location: No breaking step found. I checked Sections 1–5 line by line: (2)–(10), the kernel identity (11), the Mellin representation (12), the contour bounds (13)–(14), the residues (15)–(17), and the integral identity (19)–(20).
objection:
I found no gap that blocks the proof. What I checked:
(i) The quotations of Montgomery–Vaughan Cor. 10.4 and 10.5 (2007, Ch. 10, pp. 329–330) match the supplied PDF. Cor. 10.5 is used with A=2 for −5/8≤σ≤1/4 and |t|≥2, which is inside its hypotheses.
(ii) Bound (4): N=⌈V⌉≤3V/2 for V≥2, and V+6≤4V. The functional-equation step gives T^{3/4−σ}≤T^{11/8}, and (5) holds because Re(2s+2)∈[3/4,6] and |2t|≥4.
(iii) The local factor of H_f: expanding (1−p^{−2}z²)(a_p+u_pz+q_pz²) gives the displayed polynomial. All six bounds in (7) follow from ρ(p)≤d and ρ(p²)≤dp, which hold for p∉𝓑. 𝓑 is finite because f≥2 is nonzero. The term-by-term bound (8), (6+17d)p^{−3/2}, is correct for |z|≤p^{5/8}, and U_p bounds the finitely many factors with p∈𝓑. So H_f is bounded uniformly on the strip without strengthening P5.
(iv) Kernel (11): the residues at 0, −1, −2 are 1, −2/v and 1/v², which sum to (1−1/v)². The edge bounds are right. The sum–integral interchange on Re s=2 is justified by absolute convergence from P5 (the series converges absolutely at s=2).
(v) Contour shift: the horizontal segments are O(H³T^{−11/8})→0 for fixed H. The left-line constants are right: (13/8)(5/8)(3/8)=195/512, and ∫_2^∞ t^{−11/8}dt=(8/3)2^{−3/8}. The bound is uniform in H.
(vi) Residues: at 1, q(1)=1 and q′(1)=−3/2 give R_fH²log H+B_fH². At 0, −2D_f(0)H=cH, using D_f(0)=−c/2 from P5. At −1/2, (s−1)s(s+1)=3/8 gives −K_fH^{1/2}. The pole at −1/2 is simple (from ζ(2s+2)) and there are no other poles in −5/8≤σ≤2.
(vii) Section 5 is an exact finite computation. x/Z≥1 and x/Y≥1, so Θ_f is evaluated only on its domain.
(viii) The statement is proved as stated: real H≥1, error O(H^{3/8}), constant depending only on f. The F_f bound follows exactly.
Numerical check (not needed for the verdict): for f(t)=t²+1, (Θ_f(H)−R_fH²log H−B_fH²−cH)/H^{1/2} came out −0.13877 at H=10³ and −0.13819 at H=10⁴, against −K_f≈−0.13808. The drift at larger H comes from truncating the Euler products for R_f and B_f at 2·10⁶ primes.
No result from 2011 or later is cited, and I accessed no excluded sources.
other_issues: Cosmetic, in the proof of (11): for the horizontal segments, the bound on |v^z| over the fixed segment, max(v, v^{-N-1/2}), is not written out. It is trivial.

Cosmetic: Section 1 says ζ(s) is analytic on the negative strip and at 0 because of the functional equation. This is standard, but the proof only needs that ζ is analytic away from s=1, which is well known.
